newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Nov 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Nov 1.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- JARDINE FLEMING ACTION GROUP SEEKS REDRESS

Jardine Fleming Pacific Securities Trust is to come under pressure from an action group formed by investors to seek compensation for money lost in the fund formerly run by disgraced manager Colin Armstrong. The Pacific Securities Trust Action Group will be co-ordinated from Hong Kong but will seek the support of investors from around the world.
-- EXPORT CREDITS POSTS RECORD 246 MLN STG SURPLUS

The Export Credits Department has produced its largest surplus for over a decade after accumulating losses of 3.7 billion stg, according to the department's annual report. A cash contribution of 246 million stg will be made by the department, which is the government agency insuring large-scale overseas projects, to the Treasury. The surplus arises from a drop in claims and a sharp rise in business.
-- BRANDS HATCH LEISURE IN POLE POSITION FOR FLOAT

Brands Hatch Leisure is set to start trading shares next Thursday with the placing price fixed at 157p, capitalising the company at 34.5 million stg. The company is raising 9.3 million stg to fund expansion with the introduction of a rally school at Oulton Park being first on the agenda.
THE TIMES
-- LONRHO SELLS METROPOLE CHAIN TO STAKIS

Lonrho sold its Metropole Hotel chain to Stakis, the leisure group yesterday, for 327 million pounds stg. The sale is a big step towards the break-up of Lonrho. Stakis, is launching a 222 million stg 4-for-7 rights issue at 82p a share to part-fund the deal. Schroders, which underwrote the issue, in an unusual move, put around one-third of the total issue out to tender at commission rates below the standard 1.5 per cent rate.
-- DOWNSTREAM PRESSURES HOLD BACK SHELL PROFITS

The royal Dutch/Shell group was hit by collapsing margins in refining and chemicals despite a higher oil price. Brent crude was at its highest price since the Gulf War during Shell's third quarter and the company's three-month earnings from the sale of oil and gas nearly doubled from the previous year, but profits from chemicals and refining fell sharply.
-- BODY SHOP OFFSETS US LOSS WITH SALES GROWTH IN ASIA

Sales growth in Asia has offset a poor showing in America for the Body Shop. The company reported a pre-tax profit of 11.8 million stg for the six months to August 31, up 30 per cent on the same period last year. Total retail sales grew by 13 per cent, up 8 per cent in Asia, but down 5 per cent in the U.S.
THE GUARDIAN
-- WARBURG LANDS ONE BLN STG JAPAN DEAL

SBC Warburg looks likely win the mandate to raise 200 billion yen for Fuji Bank in Tokyo and become the first European bank to clinch a big international fund-raising deal for a leading Japanese company. The deal, to be announced in the next two weeks, will represent a breakthrough in SBC Warburg's attempt to challenge Wall Street's virtual monopoly on handling international equity offerings for large Japanese companies.
-- MURDOCH PULLS WARNER PLUG

Rupert Murdoch's News Corporation, which owns 40 per cent of the satellite network BSkyB, refused to carry Time Warner's family entertainment channel in the UK. The move is thought to be in retaliation to Time Warner's refusal to allow News Corp's all news channel Fox Television on New York cables.
-- COWIE'S 282 MLN STG OFFER FOR BRITISH BUS REFERRED TO MMC

Cowie Group's proposed takeover of British Bus was referred to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission yesterday. The 282 million stg takeover would make Cowie Britain's third-biggest bus company. The referral was made by the Government on the grounds that it could create unfair competition. The decision took the City by surprise and wiped 23 million stg off Cowie's stock market value.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- WATCHDOG BARS FIDELITY ARM FROM NEW BUSINESS

Fidelity Brokerage Services (FBS) has been barred by the Securities and Futures Authority from taking on any new business for the next three months. FBS, the UK private client stock broking arm for the giant U.S. fund management group, will also pay compensation if any of its 30,000 UK clients have suffered losses as a result of five months of problems caused by its new computer system. The SFA has given FBS until the end of January to correct its problems and will take further steps if necessary after that time.
-- WACE SHARES CRASH ON THIRD PROFITS WARNING

Problems continued for printing company Wace yesterday, when it issued a profit warning, the third of the year, along with a wholesale restructuring and an additional nine million stg of exceptional charges. Shares in Wace crashed by almost 50 per cent to 69.5p on the announcement, down from 279p in March. Poorer than expected sales in September and October have been blamed for the latest setback.
-- CBI SAYS NO TO TWO-TIER BOARDS

A report by the Confederation of British Industry (CBI) says that allowing stakeholders to be represented on company boards would raise conflicts of interest, blur lines of responsibility and create barriers between shareholders and management. The CBI warned that creating a two-tier structure, such as Labour plans to do by giving employees and customers a say in the running of companies, would not deliver greater protection for investors while robbing companies of the cohesion that the British system of unitary boards produces.
